core_obligations: The zero dimensional piece (proof lines 969-990): the structure morphism and the rational point give correspondences in degree zero between the base and the curve; their composition in one order is the identity, while the composition in the other order corresponds to the graph of the constant morphism, which is the given zero cycle; multiplying by these correspondences on both sides shows that the two compositions with the idempotent reproduce the correspondences, so they are mutually inverse morphisms of motives.

The degree two piece (proof lines 992-1028): the point and the fundamental class give correspondences in degrees one and minus one, whose composition in one order is the identity because the intersection product of the point with the curve is the point; computing the intersection product on the triple product shows that the composition in the other order is the given degree two cycle; as before, the displayed descriptions of the morphism groups exhibit the two correspondences as mutually inverse morphisms of motives.
proof_roadmap: Use the structure morphism and the rational point for the zero dimensional piece.
Compute the intersection product on the triple product for the degree two piece.
Read off mutual inverses from the descriptions of the morphism groups.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for the decomposition of the projective line over the base, the motive with the zero dimensional cycle is isomorphic to the unit motive and the motive with the degree two cycle is isomorphic to the unit motive twisted by minus one (statement lines 965-973). The proof (proof lines 974-1028) constructs the corresponding correspondences from the structure morphism, the rational point and the fundamental class, computes their compositions by intersection theory, and concludes that they are mutually inverse. H3: two isomorphism verifications with an explicit intersection product computation, written out in full.
